sources.title: AASB 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers
sources.fact: Unit of account, timing, progress, variable consideration and contract-balance principles come from the compilation operative for the reporting period.

sources.title: AASB 9 Financial Instruments
sources.fact: Contract assets sit in the expected credit loss requirements: the simplified approach in AASB 9 paras 5.5.15 to 5.5.16 covers trade receivables, contract assets and lease receivables, so every contract asset belongs in the provision matrix population. The compilation read (AASB9_12-14_COMPdec22_01-23, issued 15 December 2022) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2023 but before 1 January 2026. No loss amount or provisioning conclusion is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. For reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026, confirm the compilation amended by AASB 2024-2 at standards.aasb.gov.au before relying on paragraph numbers.

sources.title: AASB 137 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
sources.fact: Loss-making contracts are onerous-contract provisions because AASB 15 contains no onerous-contract requirements: para 66 recognises and measures the present obligation as a provision; para 68 measures unavoidable costs as the least net cost of exiting, being the lower of the cost of fulfilling the contract and any compensation or penalties for not fulfilling it; para 68A counts the cost of fulfilling a contract as its incremental costs plus an allocation of other directly related costs, for example the depreciation charge for plant used in fulfilling the contract; and para 69 requires impairment of assets used in fulfilling the contract before a separate provision. The compilation read (AASB137_08-15_COMPdec22_01-23, issued 15 December 2022) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2023 that end before 28 February 2026. No onerous conclusion or measurement is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. The compilation read ends its window at periods ending before 28 February 2026; confirm the operative compilation at standards.aasb.gov.au for later periods.

sources.title: AASB 1060 General Purpose Financial Statements – Simplified Disclosures for For-Profit and Not-for-Profit Tier 2 Entities
sources.fact: The Tier 2 disclosure set the schedule feeds: para 157 is the general disclosures about revenue, paras 158 to 159 are the disclosures relating to performance obligations satisfied over time, and para 44 is the split between information presented in the statement of financial position and in the notes. The compilation read (AASB1060_03-20_COMPmar21_07-21, issued 29 March 2021) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 July 2021 but before 1 January 2022. No disclosure conclusion is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. The operative window on the page read is narrow and the AASB portal serves later compiled text of AASB 1060; amending pronouncements AASB 2025-2 and AASB 2025-3 apply to periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026. Confirm the compilation operative for the reporting period at standards.aasb.gov.au before citing paragraph numbers.

sources.title: AASB 1053 Application of Tiers of Australian Accounting Standards
sources.fact: The tier and framework question the workflow hands to the engagement lead: AASB 1053 sets Tier 1 as Australian Accounting Standards and Tier 2 as Australian Accounting Standards – Simplified Disclosures, with Tier 2 taking the recognition and measurement requirements of Tier 1 at substantially reduced disclosures, applied through paras 11 and 13. The compilation read (AASB1053_06-10_COMPmay22_07-21, issued 2 May 2022) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 July 2021 but before 1 January 2027 that end on or after 30 June 2022. No tier or framework conclusion is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. Confirm the operative compilation and any later amending pronouncement at standards.aasb.gov.au at use time.

sources.title: AASB 108 Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors
sources.fact: The change-in-estimate treatment the checks rely on when a measure of progress changes (a change in the measure of progress is a change in accounting estimate under AASB 15 para 43, already indexed): AASB 108 paras 34 to 38 define changes in accounting estimates and require the effect to be recognised prospectively, in profit or loss in the period of the change if the change affects that period only, or in the period of the change and future periods if it affects both. The compilation read (AASB108_08-15_COMPmar21_01-23, issued 30 March 2021) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2023 but before 1 January 2027. No change-in-estimate treatment is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. Confirm the operative compilation at standards.aasb.gov.au at use time.

sources.title: ASIC Are you a large or small proprietary company
sources.fact: The company size settings behind the reporting tier decision: for financial years commencing on or after 1 July 2019 a proprietary company is large when it meets at least two of consolidated revenue of 50 million dollars or more, consolidated gross assets of 25 million dollars or more, and 100 or more employees at the end of the financial year, and a large proprietary company must prepare and lodge a financial report and a director's report, audited unless ASIC grants relief. No size or reporting conclusion is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. Thresholds are period-specific and the page records a change on 1 July 2019 and proposed further changes; read the page for the reporting period before concluding size.

sources.title: ASIC Information Sheet 31 Lodgement of financial reports
sources.fact: The current ASIC reporting guidance behind the framework conclusion: Information Sheet 31 sets out which entities must prepare and lodge financial reports under s 292 of the Corporations Act 2001 and what must be lodged; the page read states it was updated in April 2026. No lodging obligation conclusion is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. The information sheet avoids legal language and states it may contain generalisations; check the Corporations Act and the entity's own circumstances before concluding an obligation.

sources.title: ATO Taxation Ruling TR 2018/3 Income tax: tax treatment of long term construction contracts
sources.fact: The ATO position on long term construction contracts the boundary requires the preparer to confirm: the ruling covers contracts under which construction work extends beyond one year of income, gives the methods acceptable for returning the income derived and recognising the expenses incurred, and states that assessable income includes amounts billed or billable for work carried out and certified as acceptable for payment, not only amounts received. The ruling was published on 7 March 2018 and its PDF version is the authorised version. No tax treatment is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. The PDF at https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/pdf/pbr/tr2018-003.pdf is the authorised version. A draft compliance guideline (PCG 2026/D2) on Part IVA and long-term construction contracts was listed as under development when this page was read; it changes nothing in the ruling until finalised.

sources.title: Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Regulation 2020 (NSW)
sources.fact: The NSW retention money trust obligations the boundaries send the preparer to at the instrument itself: Part 2 requires a head contractor to hold retention money in trust for the subcontractor entitled to the money and to pay it into a retention money trust account with an approved ADI, as soon as possible and no later than 5 business days after being required to retain it (cl 8). The version read is the current version for 1 March 2021 to date. No retention classification is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. sources.title: Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 1999 (NSW)
sources.fact: The security of payment regime that feeds the AASB 15 para B12 entitlement analysis: the Act governs payment claims and adjudication for construction work in NSW, and s 12A enables the retention money trust requirements the Regulation imposes. The version read is the current version for 20 August 2024 to date. No entitlement or enforceability conclusion is adopted from this record.
